terms.gloss: the father as head and owner of the household; also, a plain householder
terms.grammar: noun: pater declines and familiās, the old genitive, stays as it is; plural patrēs familiās
evidence: Cato Agr. 2.1: paterfamiliās ubi ad vīllam venit (Lewis & Short)
Cic. de Or. 1.132: sīcut ūnus paterfamiliās hīs dē rēbus loquor (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Also written as two words, and with the ordinary genitive, pater familiae (Caes. BG 6.19.3). The house’s mistress is māterfamiliās.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 20, 24, checked against the searchable text of the book.
